features.title: Starting a new font
features.summary: Name the font, choose where it's saved and which languages it covers.
features.body:
When ChewPack opens you see the start screen: recent fonts on one side, a new font on the other.

For a new font, type its **family name**, pick the **folder** it's saved in, and tick the **languages** it should support. The languages decide which letters the glyph grid shows, so a font for English and Czech lists the Czech accented letters but not Greek or Cyrillic. You can change the languages any time in **Font › Languages…**.

ChewPack never overwrites a font already saved under the same name.

features.title: Saving, autosave and recovery
features.summary: Your work is a .pack project; ChewPack also keeps a recovery copy in case it crashes.
features.body:
A ChewPack font is saved as a **.pack** project file. It holds everything: outlines, metrics, kerning, features, masters and font info. Fonts you export (TTF, OTF, WOFF2…) are made *from* the project; keep the .pack to keep editing.

While you work, ChewPack keeps an **autosave** copy in the background. If the app or Windows crashes, the next start offers to recover it. A normal close clears the autosave.

features.title: Undo
features.summary: Every glyph editor has its own undo; font-wide actions have one of their own too.
features.body:
Ctrl+Z undoes your last change in the glyph you're editing. Each open glyph keeps its own history, so undoing in **a** never touches **b**.

Actions on the font as a whole (deleting, moving or renaming glyphs, changes in Font Info, a script run) are undone from the main window too. When an action can be undone, the notification that confirms it often has an **Undo** button.

features.title: The workspace
features.summary: Glyph grid, glyph tabs, tool rail, Inspector and master strip, arranged the way you like.
features.body:
The main window holds:

- **Glyph grid**: every glyph of the font, with a sidebar of sections.
- **Glyph tabs**: one tab per glyph you open. Ctrl+W closes a tab.
- **Tool rail**: the drawing tools, each with a one-letter key.
- **Inspector**: details of what's selected: points, bounds, spacing, kerning, masters and layers. Its sections fold under their headers.
- **Master strip**: the masters of the glyph, to switch between them while drawing.

The **Window** menu shows or hides each panel and the toolbar. **Window › Reset workspace** puts everything back where it started.

features.title: The Inspector
features.summary: Exact numbers for the selected point, the glyph's bounds, spacing, kerning, masters and layers.
features.body:
The Inspector shows what's selected in the glyph editor and lets you type exact values:

- **Point**: position, and whether it's a **Corner** or **Smooth** point.
- **Guide**: add a guide, an angled guide, or one at a height.
- **Bounds**: the size and position of the selection, or the whole glyph.
- **Spacing**: advance width and side bearings (LSB/RSB). These also take links like `=n`.
- **Kerning**: the glyph's kerning groups, and exceptions for a single pair.
- **Masters** and **Layers**: duplicate or delete a master's version of the glyph, and pick a background glyph.

Every number field accepts arrow keys to step the value.
verify: Arrow keys step number fields (from NumericFieldStepping; confirm the keys).

features.title: Languages and scripts
features.summary: Pick the languages the font supports; ChewPack lists the letters they need and shows your coverage.
where: Glyph grid sidebar › Add language or script…
features.body:
Instead of choosing characters one by one, you choose **languages** (Czech, Polish, Vietnamese…) and **scripts** (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic…). The glyph grid then lists exactly the letters they need.

**Font Info › Languages** shows how much of each language is drawn. In the grid's sidebar, every language that still misses letters gets a smart list **Missing for <language>**, so you can work through what's left.

features.title: The glyph grid
features.summary: Every glyph of the font, by script and section, with accented letters kept beside their base.
features.body:
The grid shows the glyphs of your font as tiles. The sidebar lists:

- **This font**: the sections of the scripts your font uses (only those).
- **Masters**: switch the master the grid shows.
- **Flags**: glyphs you marked Redraw, In progress or Approved.
- **Smart lists**: glyphs that need attention.

Accented letters sit on the same row as their base letter, so **A Á Ä Å** read together. Every glyph in the font has a home section, including ones you added yourself.

Double-click a tile to open it in a glyph tab. Right-click a tile for more, such as drafting an undrawn letter from a relative.

features.title: Flags
features.summary: Mark glyphs Redraw, In progress or Approved; the mark shows on their tiles.
features.body: A flag is your own note on a glyph. Use **Redraw** for glyphs to come back to, **In progress** for ones you're working on, and **Approved** when they're done. The flag shows on the glyph's tile, and the sidebar lists the flagged glyphs of each kind. **Clear flag** removes it.

features.title: Smart lists
features.summary: Lists that fill themselves: glyphs that need a check, glyphs made of components, letters a language still misses.
features.body:
- **Needs a check**: glyphs with something worth a look, such as points that sit a unit or two off a metric line.
- **Made of components**: glyphs built from other glyphs.
- **Missing for <language>**: one list per language that still lacks letters.

The lists update as you work.

features.title: Adding, duplicating and renaming glyphs
features.summary: Add glyphs beyond your languages, duplicate one as a starting point, change its name or Unicode value.
features.body:
**Add glyphs…** adds characters or named glyphs to the font. **Duplicate glyph…** copies a glyph under a new name; it's the usual start for an alternate like `a.ss01`. **Glyph identity…** changes a glyph's name, Unicode value and OpenType class (base, ligature, mark, component, or automatic).

Deleting a glyph can be undone from the main window.

features.title: Glyphs without a character
features.summary: Small caps, ligatures and alternates (a.sc, f_i, g.ss01) are glyphs known by name.
features.body:
Not every glyph is a character you can type. Small caps (`a.sc`), ligatures (`f_i`) and alternates (`g.ss01`) are **unencoded**: they have a name but no Unicode value, and OpenType features swap them in.

Name them with the usual suffixes and ChewPack writes the features for you (see **Automatic features**). In preview text, type a slash and the name followed by a space to show one: `/a.sc `.

features.title: Draft a glyph from its relatives
features.summary: Start b from d, u from n, m from n: a first draft to refine.
where: Glyph grid › right-click an undrawn glyph › Draft from …
features.body:
Many letters are made of the same parts. Right-click a glyph you haven't drawn and ChewPack offers drafts from letters you have:

- **b, d, p, q** are mirrors, flips and turns of each other.
- **u** is **n** upside down.
- **h** is **n** with its stem raised to the ascender.
- **m** is **n** with its arch repeated.

A draft is a starting point, not a finished letter: optical corrections are still yours to make.

features.title: Previews of undrawn letters
features.summary: Accented letters you haven't built show your base letter with a ghost accent; others show a faded stand-in.
features.body: Text you preview never has holes. An undrawn **á** shows your real **a** with the missing accent as a ghost, and takes the base letter's width and kerning. Any other undrawn character shows a faded system-font stand-in with a believable width, so a sentence keeps its rhythm. **View › Missing glyph placeholders** turns this on and off.

features.title: The tools
features.summary: Twelve tools on the rail, each with a one-letter key.
features.body:
| Tool | Key | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select | V | Click points, drag to box-select. |
| Transform | S | Drag the handles around the selection; Alt keeps proportions. |
| Slant | I | Click a pivot, drag the angle. |
| Pen | P | Click to add points, click the first point to close. |
| Rectangle | B | Drag to draw. |
| Ellipse | O | Drag to draw. |
| Knife | X | Click or drag across contours to cut; Shift cuts through. |
| Fill | F | Click a region to fill it; Alt+click makes a hole. |
| Metrics | M | Drag side bearings. |
| Kerning | K | Drag the slider between two letters. |
| Hand | H | Drag to move around. |
| Zoom | Z | Click to zoom in, Alt+click to zoom out. |

The tool keys work while the glyph editor has focus. Hover a tool for a reminder.

features.title: Pen
features.summary: Draw outlines point by point: click for corners, drag for curves.
features.body:
Click to place a corner point. Drag while placing a point to pull out its handles and make a curve. Click the first point again to close the contour.

Tips:
- Put points at the **extremes** of curves (top, bottom, left, right); fonts render best that way, and **Add points at extremes** does it for you.
- Points snap to the baseline, x-height and other metric lines, and to their overshoot zones.
- Press **Esc** to stop drawing.

features.title: Rectangle and Ellipse
features.summary: Drag out stems, bars, bowls and dots in one move.
features.body: Drag to draw a rectangle or an ellipse. Many letters start as a few overlapping shapes, a stem and a bowl say, then become one outline with **Remove overlap** (Ctrl+M).

features.title: Knife
features.summary: Cut contours along a line.
features.body: Click or drag across contours to cut them where the line crosses. Hold **Shift** to cut through, splitting the shape into separate pieces.
verify: Exact Shift behaviour ('cuts through' per the tooltip; code calls it splitContours).

features.title: Fill
features.summary: Click a region to fill it, Alt+click to make it a hole.
features.body:
Where contours overlap or sit inside each other, the Fill tool decides which regions are ink. Click a region to fill it; **Alt+click** to make it a hole. The preview shows the change before you click.

Ink in a font comes from the direction contours run (outer shapes one way, holes the other). The Fill tool sets that for you, so you never have to reverse a contour by hand.

features.title: Transform, slant, flip and rotate
features.summary: Scale, slant, mirror and turn selections.
features.body:
**Transform** puts handles around the selection: drag them to scale, hold **Alt** to keep proportions. **Slant** slants around a pivot: click the pivot, then drag the angle. Handy for a first pass at an italic.

**E** flips the selection horizontally, **W** vertically, **R** rotates it 90° clockwise. Flipping keeps filled shapes filled.

features.title: Points and handles
features.summary: Select, nudge, make corners or smooth points, add handles to straight lines.
features.body:
- **Click** a point to select it, **Shift+click** to add to the selection, **drag** to box-select.
- **Double-click** a segment to select its whole contour.
- **Arrow keys** nudge by 1 unit, **Shift+arrows** by 10.
- **Alt+click** a straight segment to give it handles and turn it into a curve.
- **Contour › Make points corners** (Ctrl+Alt+G) and **Make points smooth** (Ctrl+Alt+N) change selected points; the Inspector has the same switch.
- While dragging a point, it snaps to metric lines and overshoot zones; hold **Alt** to snap to the plain lines only.

features.title: Selection actions
features.summary: Press Q for the actions that fit what you've selected, right above it.
features.body: Select points or contours and press **Q** (or right-click them): a small bar floats above the selection with the actions that apply, so you don't have to hunt through menus. With nothing selected, Q tells you how it works.

features.title: Tunni lines
features.summary: Balance a curve's two handles with one line.
features.body: A Tunni line joins the ends of a curve's two handles. Dragging it changes both handles together, keeping the curve's balance. It's a quick way to make a curve fuller or flatter. Press **L** to show or hide them.
verify: Whether Tunni lines can be dragged in ChewPack or are display-only.

features.title: Measurements
features.summary: See distances and handle lengths on the canvas.
features.body: **View › Measurements** shows measurement arrows on the canvas, to check stem widths and distances at a glance. In **Settings**, you can also show **handle length labels** and set the arrow length.

features.title: Guides
features.summary: Horizontal, vertical and angled guides to line things up.
features.body: Add a guide from the Inspector: a plain **Guide**, an **Angled** one (useful for italics and diagonals), or one at a **Height** you type. Drag a guide to move it. Guides help you draw; they're not exported.
verify: Guides can also be dragged out of rulers (code mentions fromRuler).

features.title: Background glyph
features.summary: Draw over another glyph shown faintly behind, such as r behind ř.
features.body: Pick another glyph to show faintly behind the one you're drawing. It lines up at the left edge, as the two would in text. For an accented or extra letter, its base letter is offered in one click. It's a drawing aid only: nothing of it is exported, and it follows along if you change the glyph behind.

features.title: Components and anchors
features.summary: Build glyphs from other glyphs, and mark where accents attach.
features.body:
A **component** is a live copy of another glyph: build **é** from **e** plus an accent and it updates whenever you change **e**. **Decompose** turns a component into ordinary outlines.

An **anchor** is a named point that marks where things attach: `top` on a letter, `_top` on an accent. Anchors place accents when you build letters, and ChewPack exports them as OpenType mark positioning, so apps can stack accents on any letter.

features.title: Near-miss alignment check
features.summary: Points that sit 1–3 units off a metric line are flagged: slips you can't see by eye.
features.body:
A point 2 units below the x-height is almost always a mistake, and invisible on screen. ChewPack finds points that sit *almost* on a metric line or overshoot edge (about 3 units at 1000 UPM) and marks them on the canvas, in the Inspector ("2 units below the x-height"), in the **Needs a check** smart list, and when you check the font. Points along a sloped part of a curve are left alone, since they're never meant to sit on a line.

It's a warning, never an error: some designs miss a line on purpose.

features.title: Live preview
features.summary: A line of text under the editor shows the glyph in context while you draw.
features.body: Below the canvas, a line of set type shows the glyph you're editing (in the accent colour) between letters you've drawn, the way type designers proof a letter. It updates as you drag. If that's slow on a big font, turn off **View › Live preview updates**: previews then update when you let go.

features.title: Remove overlap, subtract, intersect, exclude
features.summary: Merge overlapping shapes into one outline, or cut one shape with another.
features.body:
- **Remove overlap** (Ctrl+M): overlapping shapes become one clean outline.
- **Subtract**: cut the top shape out of the one below.
- **Intersect**: keep only where shapes overlap.
- **Exclude**: keep where they don't overlap.

Overlaps are fine while drawing; remove them before you finish.

features.title: Add points at extremes
features.summary: Put a point at the top, bottom, left and right of every curve.
features.body: Fonts render and hint best when every curve has points at its extremes, where it's horizontal or vertical. This adds them without changing the shape.

features.title: Offset path
features.summary: Make contours bolder or thinner, and turn open paths into strokes.
features.body:
Offset moves every point of a contour outward (bolder) or inward (thinner) by a distance in font units. Holes shrink as the ink grows. Curve handles scale with their curve, so round shapes stay round.

An **open path** becomes a closed outline of the stroke width you choose, with flat or round ends. Draw a skeleton with the Pen and give it weight.

features.title: Round corners
features.summary: Round the selected corners, or every corner of the glyph.
features.body: Choose a radius and ChewPack rounds the selected corners, or all corners of the glyph if nothing is selected. Good for soft and rounded designs.

features.title: Paste contours from FontLab
features.summary: Bring outlines copied in FontLab into ChewPack.
where: File › Import › Paste contours from FontLab
features.body: Copy contours in FontLab, then choose **File › Import › Paste contours from FontLab** to paste them into the glyph you're editing.

features.title: Side bearings and width
features.summary: The white space on each side of a letter, which sets how text looks.
features.body:
Each glyph has a **left side bearing** (LSB), a **right side bearing** (RSB) and an **advance width**. Type them in the Inspector, or drag them with the **Metrics** tool.

Changing a side bearing moves the glyph's edge, not its drawing: the outline stays where it is and the advance grows or shrinks.

A common way to start: space **n** and **o** by hand, then base everything else on them, by linking or with auto-spacing.

features.title: Linked side bearings
features.summary: Make a side bearing follow another glyph's, so changing n respaces every letter that shares its stem.
features.body:
Type a glyph into the LSB or RSB field. With an equals sign the side stays **linked** and follows the source whenever it changes. A linked side shows the link and its current value, e.g. `=n (37)`.

| You type | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `=n` | Link: this side follows the same side of n. |
| `=\|o` | Link to the opposite side: on a glyph's right, follows o's left. |
| `=n+10` | Link with an offset: n's value plus 10. |
| `n` | Copy once: take n's value now, without linking. |
| `42` | A number. On a linked side, it changes the glyph the chain starts from. |
| *(empty)* | Unlink: keep the current value. |

Link a family to one source (n's left side drives m, h, r, p) and respace them all by changing n.

features.title: Auto-spacing
features.summary: Optical side bearings for the whole font, measured from your hand-spaced n and o.
features.body:
Space **n** and **o** (and **H** and **O** for capitals) by hand first. Auto-space then measures the white each letter already has on its sides (an **o** curves away, an **n** stem doesn't) and proposes side bearings that give every letter the same amount of space. The method follows the area method behind HT Letterspacer.

You see the proposal in sample text before applying it. **Revert auto-spacing** puts the old values back.

features.title: Vertical metrics
features.summary: Units per em, ascender, descender, x-height, cap height and line gap.
features.body: These numbers, in font units, are shared by every glyph: **units per em** (the size of the design grid, usually 1000), **ascender**, **descender**, **cap height**, **x-height** and **line gap**. They set where metric lines sit in the editor and how much room apps give each line of text.

features.title: Overshoots and alignment zones
features.summary: Round letters reach a little past the lines; zones let points snap there.
features.body: Round letters like **o** dip slightly below the baseline and rise above the x-height so they look the same size as flat ones. These **overshoots** have zones; points snap into them while you draw. In OTF export, the zones become blue zones that help small sizes render evenly.

features.title: Kerning tool
features.summary: Adjust the space between two specific letters by dragging.
features.body:
Kerning fixes pairs that spacing alone can't, such as **To**, **AV** or **LT**. With the Kerning tool, drag the green slider between two letters. The arrow keys nudge by 1 unit, **Shift+arrows** by 10, and **Shift** while dragging rounds to tens.

Kerning applies to the letters' groups if they have them. Use **Exception for this pair** in the Inspector to kern one pair differently from its group.

features.title: Kerning groups
features.summary: Letters with the same side shape kern alike: kern O once, and C, G, Q follow.
features.body:
Each glyph can belong to a group on its **left** side and on its **right** side. **O, C, G, Q** share a round left side, so put them in one left group, and a pair kerned with that group applies to all of them. Exported fonts store this as class kerning, which keeps them small.

**Exception for this pair** kerns a single pair differently from its groups.

features.title: Group accented letters for kerning
features.summary: Put Á, Ä, Å into the kerning groups of A in one step.
where: Font › Group accented letters for kerning…
features.body: Accented letters should usually kern like their base letter. This puts every accented letter into its base letter's groups, so you don't kern **Ä** separately from **A**.

features.title: Kerning pairs list
features.summary: Every kerning pair in one list: find, sort, correct and clean up.
features.body: The Kerning tool shows one pair at a time; this window shows them all. Search, sort by value, edit a value (Enter applies, Esc puts the old one back), and delete pairs you no longer need. Each pair is previewed between letters of its case. All edits in one session undo together.

features.title: Kerning suggestions
features.summary: ChewPack measures the white between letters and suggests pairs to tighten.
features.body:
Kerning suggestions compare each pair with how your hand-spaced pairs read (**nn, no, oo** for lowercase, **HH, HO, OO** for capitals). A pair whose narrowest gap is wider than its references gets a suggestion to tighten it by part of the difference. Suggestions only tighten; pairs that come too close are left to spacing.

You review the suggestions and choose which to apply.
verify: Exact location of the suggestions button within the Kerning pairs window.

features.title: OpenType features
features.summary: Ligatures, small caps, figures and stylistic sets, written in feature code.
features.body:
Features tell apps when to swap glyphs: **liga** turns f + i into a ligature, **smcp** uses small caps, **ss01** switches on a stylistic set. ChewPack compiles the standard AFDKO feature language (`.fea`), the same one used by other font editors, and shows errors before you export.

Most fonts need little or no code: name your glyphs well and ChewPack writes the common features itself.

features.title: Automatic features
features.summary: Name a glyph a.sc, f_i or g.ss01 and the feature is written for you.
features.body: ChewPack writes features from glyph names: `.sc` suffixes give small caps, names like `f_i` give ligatures, `.ss01`–`.ss20` give stylistic sets, and so on. Code you write yourself takes precedence for the same feature. You can turn automatic features off and see the code they produce.

features.title: Mark positioning from anchors
features.summary: Anchors become OpenType mark and mkmk, so apps can place any accent on any letter.
features.body: Put a `top` anchor on letters and a `_top` anchor on combining accents, and the exported font includes **mark** positioning: apps can put the accent on letters you never built. Marks with both `_top` and `top` stack on each other (**mkmk**), as Vietnamese needs.

features.title: Masters
features.summary: Draw a light and a bold version of the font and blend everything in between.
features.body:
A **master** is a complete version of the font at one weight, say Light (300) and Bold (700). Each master has a place on the weight axis. You draw each glyph in every master; ChewPack blends between them.

To blend, a glyph's masters must **match**: the same contours, points and handles in the same order. The usual way is to duplicate a master and then move points rather than redraw. Font Info › Masters lists glyphs that don't match, and why.

The master strip and the glyph grid's sidebar switch the master you're editing.

features.title: Instances
features.summary: Named styles between the masters, such as Medium at 500, exported as their own fonts.
features.body: An **instance** is a named style at a weight between your masters: Regular at 400, Medium at 500, SemiBold at 600. Export can write every instance as its own font file ("Family-Medium.ttf"). A glyph whose masters don't match is taken from the nearer master and reported.

features.title: Python scripting
features.summary: Automate repetitive work with Python 3.13, built in. No installation needed.
features.body:
ChewPack comes with Python. Write a few lines to set the spacing of 80 glyphs, build accented letters, rename a set or list what's still empty. The API follows FontParts (RoboFont, FontLab), so many existing scripts work with small changes.

Saved scripts appear in the **Scripts** menu and run in one click. Everything a run changes undoes with one Ctrl+Z.

See the full **Scripting in ChewPack** guide for a first script, copy-ready recipes and the complete API.

features.title: Opening existing fonts
features.summary: Open TTF, OTF, WOFF, WOFF2 and TTC fonts as editable projects.
features.body:
ChewPack opens **TTF, OTF (CFF and CFF2), WOFF, WOFF2** and **TTC/OTC** collections (the first font) as a new project, with outlines, metrics, kerning and features. A **variable font** opens at its default style.

Only open fonts you have the right to modify; check the font's licence.

features.title: Exporting fonts
features.summary: TrueType, OpenType, WOFF2, WOFF for the web, and UFO or VFJ sources for other editors.
features.body:
Export opens a sheet under the toolbar: pick a format card, the file name and the folder.

| Format | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| **TrueType (.ttf)** | The most widely supported desktop format. |
| **OpenType (.otf)** | Desktop; keeps your curves exactly as drawn (CFF outlines). |
| **WOFF2 (.woff2)** | Websites. The smallest web font. |
| **WOFF (.woff)** | Websites, for older browsers. |
| **UFO (.ufo)** | Source format for Glyphs, FontLab, RoboFont and fontmake. |
| **FontLab VFJ (.vfj)** | Source format for FontLab. |

With several masters, export can write every instance. Before writing, ChewPack checks the font and asks once if there are warnings. When it's done, a notification offers **Show** to open the folder.

features.title: Check font
features.summary: Find problems before you export: missing names, broken features, near-miss points, a missing space.

features.title: Hinting
features.summary: Automatic hints for crisp small sizes: stem hints and blue zones in OTF, smoothing in TTF.
features.body: You don't have to hint anything. **OTF** exports get PostScript stem hints and blue zones from your alignment zones. **TTF** exports ask Windows to smooth the font (a `gasp` table) rather than carry TrueType instructions. Points at curve extremes help hinting most.

features.title: Font info
features.summary: Names, version, credits, licence, metrics, classification, zones, masters and languages.
features.body:
Font Info has a page for each part of the font:

- **Names**: family name, version, designer, manufacturer (with URLs), vendor ID, trademark, copyright, description, licence and licence URL. Apps and font managers show these.
- **Metrics**: units per em, ascender, descender, cap height, x-height, line gap.
- **Classification**: weight (1–1000), width (1–9) and slope (upright, italic, oblique), which apps use to sort styles in a family.
- **Zones**: overshoots and alignment zones.
- **Masters**: the weight axis, masters and instances.
- **Languages**: languages and scripts, with coverage.

Changes here undo from the main window.

features.title: Proofing workspace
features.summary: Set your own text at any size, compare it side by side, and try features on and off.
features.body: Type any **proof text** and see it at several **sizes**. Set the text and paper colours of each side to compare (say, dark on light against light on dark), add a **comparison text**, and switch **features** on and off by tag to check ligatures, small caps or stylistic sets. Undrawn letters show as stand-ins so the text still reads.

features.title: Print proof and PDF
features.summary: A printable proof: name and version, a waterfall, text in each language, the character set.
features.body: Print proof lays out the font's name and version, a **waterfall** (one line per size), a sentence in each language the font covers, and every drawn glyph. It prints through the Windows print dialog; choose **Microsoft Print to PDF** for a PDF to share. Undrawn letters print as gaps, and the caption says why.

features.title: Command palette
features.summary: Ctrl+K: find any command or glyph by typing.
where: Help › Find a command or glyph… (Ctrl+K)
features.body: Press **Ctrl+K** and type: a command ("overlap", "export") runs it, a glyph name or character opens that glyph. Every menu command is there, with its shortcut, so the palette is also a quick way to learn the keys.

features.title: Keyboard shortcuts window
features.summary: F1 shows every shortcut, with a filter, in a window that can stay open.
features.body: F1 opens a list of every shortcut: those in the menus and the canvas gestures no menu shows. Type to filter. The window can stay open beside your work; Esc closes it.

features.title: Appearance
features.summary: Light, or a dark interface where letters stay on white paper.
features.body: Choose **Light** (white everywhere) or **Dark interface, white canvas**: menus, panels and dialogs go dark, while letters stay on white paper so they look the size and weight they print. The change applies immediately.

features.title: Settings
features.summary: Canvas background, measurements, previews and appearance.
features.body:
- **General / Editing**: show a reference when a glyph is empty, handle length labels, measurement arrows and their length, space for the preview, open a single glyph in an existing window.
- **Canvas background**: a grid when zoomed in and dots otherwise, grid always, dots always, or nothing.
- **Appearance**: light or dark interface.
verify: Which options sit on which Settings tab (General / Canvas / Editing / Appearance).

guides.title: Draw your first letter
guides.summary: Start a font, draw a lowercase a, clean it up and space it.

steps.title: Start a new font
steps.text: Choose New font, give it a name and tick the languages you want. The glyph grid then lists only the letters those languages need.

steps.title: Open the a
steps.text: Find a in the glyph grid and open it. The baseline, x-height and other metric lines are already drawn, with zones for overshoots.

steps.title: Draw the bowl with the Pen
steps.text: Click to place corner points, drag to pull out curves, and click the first point to close the contour. Put points at the top, bottom, left and right of the curve.

steps.title: Add the stem
steps.text: Draw a rectangle for the stem so it overlaps the bowl. The overlap is fine for now.

steps.title: Remove overlap
steps.text: Select everything and merge the shapes into one clean outline.

steps.title: Add points at extremes
steps.text: Make sure every curve has points at its extremes; fonts render best that way.

steps.title: Check it in text
steps.text: Look at the live preview under the canvas. Hold Space to see the letter without points.

steps.title: Space it
steps.text: Set the left and right side bearings in the Inspector. Once n is drawn, type =n to link a side to it.

guides.title: Space and kern
guides.summary: Space n and o by hand, let the rest follow, then kern the pairs that still need it.

steps.title: Space n and o by hand
steps.text: With the Metrics tool, adjust n and o until nnonnoo reads evenly. Everything else is measured against them, so take your time.

steps.title: Link the obvious relatives
steps.text: Type =n into the left side of m, h, r and p, and =o into the sides of c, d, e, q where they match.

steps.title: Auto-space the rest
steps.text: Font › Auto-space proposes side bearings for the remaining letters from your n and o. Compare the preview, then apply; Revert auto-spacing undoes it.

steps.title: Group letters that kern alike
steps.text: Put O, C, G, Q in a left group, and use Group accented letters for kerning so Á and Ä kern like A.

steps.title: Kern the problem pairs
steps.text: With the Kerning tool, drag the slider in pairs like To, AV and LT. Shift+arrows nudge by 10.

steps.title: Review everything in one list
steps.text: Font › Kerning pairs lists every pair: sort, correct, clean up, and review the suggestions.

guides.title: Put your font on a website
guides.summary: Check the font, export WOFF2 and use it with @font-face.

steps.title: Fill in the names
steps.text: In Font Info › Names, set the family name, version, designer and licence. Browsers and font tools show them.

steps.title: Check the font
steps.text: Font › Check font lists anything that would go wrong: a missing space, features that don't compile, points just off a line.

steps.title: Export WOFF2
steps.text: Press Ctrl+E and choose the WOFF2 card: the smallest format, supported by every current browser.

steps.title: Upload and use it
steps.text: Put the .woff2 file on your server and declare it with @font-face, then use the family name in font-family.

steps.title: Proof it
steps.text: Before shipping, check the font in the Proofing workspace at real sizes, or print a PDF proof.

guides.title: Your first script
guides.summary: Run three lines of Python that respace a selection, then undo them.

steps.title: Open the Scripting window
steps.text: Choose Scripts › Scripting window.

steps.title: Select some glyphs
steps.text: In the glyph grid, select a few glyphs whose spacing you want to set.

steps.title: Write the script
steps.text: Replace the text in the editor with this.

steps.title: Run it
steps.text: Press Ctrl+Enter. The selected glyphs now have 40 units on each side.

steps.title: Undo it
steps.text: Press Ctrl+Z in the main window: the whole run undoes in one step.
